Here's the file-level split, anchored to the large_file evidence (310 LOC at 1.0× threshold, 5 top-level functions per `crime_00026`).

## Proposed layout

Convert `src/billing.ts` into a `src/billing/` directory:

| New file | Moves | LOC est. | Evidence link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/billing/types.ts` | `User`, `InvoiceLine`, `Invoice` (L4–31) | ~28 | Five top-level functions all reference these — the natural shared base. |
| `src/billing/tax.ts` | `tax()` (L257–268) | ~12 | One of the 5 functions. Exposes the duplicate of `generateInvoice`'s L145–154 rate block so it can be deduped later. |
| `src/billing/upgrade.ts` | `recommendUpgrade()` (L272–305) | ~34 | One of the 5 functions. Independent policy (plan → next plan); shares only `User`. Owns one `Date.now()` from `crime_00019`. |
| `src/billing/refund.ts` | `calculateRefundPreview()` + the L39 comment (L33–44) | ~12 | One of the 5 functions. Carries `crime_00021` (misleading name + `saveRefundAudit`/`sendRefundEmail` side effects) and `crime_00027` (prose rule "Only owners can refund enterprise…") — keeps the False-Identity finding scoped to one module. |
| `src/billing/invoice.ts` | `generateInvoice()` (L50–253) + `listRecentInvoices()` (L307–310) | ~210 | The remaining two functions. Still hosts `crime_00005` (God Function) and 6 of the 7 `Date.now()` calls — a separate, function-level refactor. |
| `src/billing/index.ts` | `export *` re-export | ~5 | Keeps `import … from "./billing"` working. |

After the move, only `invoice.ts` will sit near the 300-line threshold; `types.ts`, `tax.ts`, `upgrade.ts`, `refund.ts` are all comfortably under, so the **`large_file` finding on `src/billing.ts` should clear**.

## Order (smallest blast radius first)

1. **`types.ts`** — pure type move, no runtime behaviour. Verify with `pnpm typecheck`.
2. **`tax.ts`** — pure function, no imports. Easiest to validate in isolation.
3. **`upgrade.ts`** — depends only on `User`. Independent of invoice flow.
4. **`refund.ts`** — depends on `User`, `Invoice`, and the (already-undefined) `saveRefundAudit`/`sendRefundEmail`. Carry the L39 comment with the function so `crime_00027`'s rule and target stay co-located.
5. **`invoice.ts`** — last and largest. Once this lands, `tax.ts` can be imported and the inline L145–154 country-rate ladder collapses to a single `tax(user.country, afterDiscount)` call. That dedupe is part of this step, not a follow-up.
6. **`index.ts`** — re-export the public surface: `generateInvoice`, `tax`, `recommendUpgrade`, `calculateRefundPreview`, `listRecentInvoices`.

## Callers to update

Grep across the fixture finds **zero in-repo callers** of any of the five exports (`generateInvoice`, `tax`, `recommendUpgrade`, `calculateRefundPreview`, `listRecentInvoices`). `src/billing.test.ts` is a stub that doesn't import the module. So:

- **No call-site edits required** inside this fixture.
- For an equivalent real repo: the `src/billing/index.ts` re-export keeps `import { generateInvoice } from "./billing"` working unchanged. A follow-up pass can tighten callers to import from the leaf modules (`./billing/invoice`, etc.) and then drop the shim.

## What this split does *not* fix (called out so it's not silently inherited)

- **`crime_00005` God Function** — `generateInvoice` is still 204 lines after the move. Needs function-level extraction (identity/metadata, plan pricing, loyalty discount, promo, risk scoring, tax, currency, persistence, audit, metrics, email, retry — twelve cohesion islands already comment-flagged in the source). Separate change.
- **`crime_00019` Temporal Recklessness** — 6 of 7 `Date.now()`/`new Date()` calls stay in `invoice.ts`; one moves to `upgrade.ts`. Clock injection is independent.
- **`crime_00010` enterprise literal scatter** — `"enterprise"` still hardcoded in `invoice.ts` pricing ladder. Resolving that needs a shared `plans.ts` constant referenced by `billing.ts`, `src/api/plan.ts`, `src/jobs/plan-sync.ts`, `src/ui/pricing.ts` — out of scope for the file split.

## Post-edit check

Re-scan with `crimes scan src/billing --format json` after step 5 and confirm `crime_00026` no longer appears on `src/billing.ts` (or its successor). `crime_00005`, `crime_00019`, `crime_00021`, `crime_00027` will move with their functions, not disappear — that's expected for a file-level split.
